title: Towards the development of machine learning models to predict protein-protein interaction modulators
abstract: Protein-protein interaction (PPI) inhibitors have a continued and increasing role in drug discovery. It is hypothesized that machine learning (ML) algorithms are able to classify or identify PPI inhibitors. In this work, we describe the performance of different algorithms broadly used in chemoinformatics to develop a classification model able to identify PPI inhibitors based on structural and physicochemical descriptors. We found that the classification algorithms have different performance according to different features employed in the training process: random forest (RF) models with the extended connectivity fingerprint radius 4 (ECFP4) had the best classification performance as compared to those models trained with ECFP6 o MACCS keys (166-bits). In general, logistic regression models had lower performance metrics than RF models, but ECFP4 was the representation most appropriate for linear regression. ECFP4 also yielded models with high performance metrics, in particular, with support vector machine (SVM). As part of this work, we constructed ensemble models based on the top-performing models. The pipeline code developed in this work and all results are freely available at https://github.com/BarbaraDiazE/PPI_ML.
